findings.message: 7 jobs start in the same minute at 00:00 (lines 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 20, 21); this happens 7 time(s) in the 7d window; the top of the hour (especially midnight) is the busiest minute on most systems
findings.fix: stagger the start minutes (e.g. 3, 17, 34, 48) or add a random delay such as: sleep $((RANDOM \% 300)); cmd

findings.message: in America/New_York when DST starts clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00, so runs at 02:00 may be skipped; when DST ends clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00, so runs at 01:00 may happen twice (behaviour depends on the cron implementation)
findings.fix: schedule the job outside the transition window (e.g. 03:30 or later) or set CRON_TZ=UTC for it

findings.message: 3 unescaped % in the command; cron turns the first one into a newline and sends the rest to stdin, so the shell only runs: /usr/bin/pg_dump app > /backups/app-$(date +
in America/New_York when DST starts clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00, so runs at 02:30 may be skipped (behaviour depends on the cron implementation)
findings.fix: schedule the job outside the transition window (e.g. 03:30 or later) or set CRON_TZ=UTC for it

findings.message: schedule "0 0 31 2 *" can never fire: no selected month has the selected day-of-month
findings.fix: pick a day that exists in the selected months (February has at most 29 days; April, June, September and November have 30)

findings.message: day-of-month "1-7" and day-of-week "MON" are both restricted, so cron runs the job when EITHER matches (on day-of-month 1-7 and also on every day-of-week MON), not only when both match
findings.fix: to require both, set day-of-week to * and test the weekday in the command, e.g. [ "$(date +\%u)" = 1 ] && cmd

findings.message: in America/New_York when DST starts clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00, so runs at 02:00 ... 02:56 (9 runs) may be skipped; when DST ends clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00, so runs at 01:00 ... 01:56 (9 runs) may happen twice (behaviour depends on the cron implementation)
findings.fix: schedule the job outside the transition window (e.g. 03:30 or later) or set CRON_TZ=UTC for it

findings.message: */7 in the minute field fires at 0,7,14,21,28,35,42,49,56; after 56 it wraps to 0, a gap of 4 minute(s) instead of 7
findings.fix: use a step that divides 60 evenly (*/2, */3, */4, */5, */6, */10, */12, */15, */20, */30) or list the exact values

findings.message: in America/New_York when DST starts clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00, so runs at 02:00 ... 02:59 (60 runs) may be skipped; when DST ends clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00, so runs at 01:00 ... 01:59 (60 runs) may happen twice (behaviour depends on the cron implementation)
findings.fix: schedule the job outside the transition window (e.g. 03:30 or later) or set CRON_TZ=UTC for it

findings.message: job runs every minute (up to 1440 times a day)
findings.fix: if this is intended, make sure the job finishes well within a minute (or use flock); otherwise pick a specific minute or a step like */5

findings.message: hour field "25": value 25 out of range 0-23
findings.fix: valid ranges: minute 0-59, hour 0-23, day-of-month 1-31, month 1-12 or JAN-DEC, day-of-week 0-7 or SUN-SAT

findings.message: "python3" is not an absolute path and PATH is not set; cron's default PATH is usually only /usr/bin:/bin
findings.fix: use the full path (find it with: command -v python3) or add PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin at the top of the crontab

findings.message: output is not redirected and MAILTO is not set; cron mails it to the local user, where it piles up unread or is lost if no MTA is installed
findings.fix: append ">> /var/log/job.log 2>&1", or set MAILTO=you@example.com (MAILTO="" to discard output)

findings.message: same schedule and command as line 26; the job runs twice every time
findings.fix: remove one of the two lines

findings.message: day-of-month field "L": "L" is a Quartz/AWS extension (L/W); this is not supported by standard cron
findings.fix: for the last day of the month use 28-31 and test it in the command: [ "$(date -d tomorrow +\%d)" = 01 ] && cmd
